items.prompt: In the video, Ate Pat said "touch your ilong". Ilong means your...
items.explanation: Ilong means nose. When Ate Pat said "touch your ilong", she wanted us to touch our nose!

items.prompt: What does the word "tenga" mean?
items.explanation: Tenga means ear. "Touch your tenga" means touch your ear!

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means eyes?
items.explanation: Mata means eyes. In the Simon Says game, Ate Pat said "eyes" and the Tagalog word is mata.

items.prompt: How do you say "hi, how are you?" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Kamusta means hi, how are you! You can say it to greet a friend, just like Ate Pat said hi to Sam.

items.prompt: Ate Pat said "po" is...
items.explanation: Po is a sign of respect. You add it to a phrase when you talk to adults or want to be polite.

items.prompt: How do you say "I'm doing fine" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Mabuti po means I'm doing fine. You can say it when someone asks how you are.

items.prompt: You come home from school feeling hungry. Which Tagalog phrase can you say to your parents?
items.explanation: Gutom na po ako means I'm hungry! The video said you can tell your parents this when you want a snack.

items.prompt: What does "masaya" mean?
items.explanation: Masaya means happy. Ate Pat said she is masaya because she loves spending time with friends!

items.prompt: This animal is pink, lives on a farm, and says "oink oink". What is it called in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Baboy means pig! The pink farm animal that says oink is baboy in Tagalog.

items.prompt: What does the color "pula" mean?
items.explanation: Pula means red. Ate Pat colored the jeepney pula, and apples are pula too!

items.prompt: The video said the "kalabaw" is the national animal of the Philippines. Kalabaw means...
items.explanation: Kalabaw means water buffalo. The kalabaw is the national animal of the Philippines!

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means dog?
items.explanation: Aso means dog. The video taught "aso" for the letter A!

items.prompt: What does "bulaklak" mean?
items.explanation: Bulaklak means flower. We learned bulaklak with the letter B!

items.prompt: What does "tubig" mean?
items.explanation: Tubig means water. The captions wrote "tuig", but the word from the video is tubig — water!

items.prompt: The video said "Ang saging ay dilaw". Saging means...
items.explanation: Saging means banana. "Ang saging ay dilaw" means the banana is yellow!

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means elephant?
items.explanation: Elepante means elephant. We learned it with the letter E!

items.prompt: What does "araw" mean? The video said it can mean sun or...
items.explanation: Araw means sun or day. The sun gives us light during the araw!

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means head?
items.explanation: Ulo means head. The video taught ulo with the letter U!

items.prompt: At the end of the video, Ate Pat said goodbye. What does "paalam" mean?
items.explanation: Paalam means goodbye! You can say paalam when you leave.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means thank you?
items.explanation: Salamat means thank you. Say salamat when someone helps you!

items.prompt: Ate Pat said "Gusto ko ng hamburger" to say she wants a hamburger. What does "gusto" mean?
items.explanation: Gusto means to want. "Gusto ko ng hamburger" means I want a hamburger!

items.prompt: You are thirsty and want a glass of water. How do you say "I want some water" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Gusto ko ng tubig means I want some water. Tubig is the Tagalog word for water!

items.prompt: In the family lesson, Ate Pat taught the word for father. "Tatay" means...
items.explanation: Tatay means father. Tatay and nanay are your parents!

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word is for an older sister? You can also use it for an older girl friend or cousin.
items.explanation: Ate means older sister. You can also call an older girl friend or cousin "ate"!

items.prompt: What does "lola" mean?
items.explanation: Lola means grandmother. Lolo and lola are your grandparents!

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means cousin?
items.explanation: Pinsan means cousin. Pinsans are the children of your aunts and uncles!

items.prompt: In the Philippines, children show respect by touching an adult's hand to their forehead. What is this called?
items.explanation: Mano po is the respectful gesture of touching an adult's hand to your forehead to ask for a blessing!

items.prompt: This farm animal is black and white, makes milk, and says "moo". What is it called in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Baka means cow! The black-and-white animal that makes milk is the baka.

items.prompt: This animal has soft, fluffy wool and says "ba ba". What is it called in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Tupa means lamb! The fluffy wool animal that says "ba ba" is the tupa.

items.prompt: Ate Pat counted flowers in the garden: isa, dalawa, tatlo, apat... What number is "lima"?
items.explanation: Lima means five! We counted isa, dalawa, tatlo, apat, lima — that's five flowers.

items.prompt: During the exercise, Ate Pat said, "In Tagalog, to jump is..." Which word did she teach?
items.explanation: Tumalon means to jump! We did jumping jacks and said "tumalon, tumalon"!

items.prompt: What does "maligo" mean?
items.explanation: Maligo means to take a bath. It was one of the action words on the flashcards!

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means to read?
items.explanation: Magbasa means to read. Magbasa is what you do with your favorite books!

items.prompt: What does "kumain" mean?
items.explanation: Kumain means to eat! "Gusto kong kumain" means I want to eat.

items.prompt: You want to ask your friend what they are doing. What can you say in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Anong ginagawa mo means what are you doing! Anong means what, ginagawa means doing, and mo means you.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means to dance?
items.explanation: Sumayaw means to dance! In video charades, the clip showed someone dancing for sumayaw.

items.prompt: Ate Pat colored the basketball hoop brown. What does "kayumanggi" mean?
items.explanation: Kayumanggi means brown. The basketball hoop was colored kayumanggi!

items.prompt: What is the most popular sport in the Philippines, according to the video?
items.explanation: Basketball is the most popular sport in the Philippines. They even have their own league called the PBA!

items.prompt: Arnis is the national martial arts form of the Philippines. What do people use in arnis?
items.explanation: In arnis, people use weapon-based fighting with sticks or knives. It was made to fight off invaders!

items.prompt: The video starts with Ate Pat saying "Kamusta". What does it mean?
items.explanation: Kamusta means hello, how are you! It's a friendly greeting.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means dog (from the first words, counting, and colors video)?
items.explanation: Aso means dog! In the video we heard "aso" after the animal that says woof.

items.prompt: In the counting part, the video said "isa, lima, anim, pito...". What number is "pito"?
items.explanation: Pito means seven! The video counted isa, lima, anim, pito — one, five, six, seven.

items.prompt: What number does "sampu" mean?
items.explanation: Sampu means ten! It's the last number when you count to ten in Tagalog.

items.prompt: What does "opo" mean?
items.explanation: Opo means yes. You can answer opo to say yes politely!

items.prompt: What does "hindi po" mean?
items.explanation: Hindi po means no. Opo means yes, and hindi po means no!

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means thank you (from the first words, counting, and colors video)?
items.explanation: Salamat means thank you. Say "salamat po" to be extra polite!

items.prompt: The video said "Nana, Mama, Mommy". Which Tagalog word means mommy?
items.explanation: Nanay means mommy! "Nana, mama, mommy" are all ways to call the person who takes care of you.

items.prompt: In the body parts part, the video said "mata, ilong, bibig, tenga". What does "mata" mean?
items.explanation: Mata means eye! Mata, ilong, bibig, tenga — eye, nose, mouth, ear.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means to dance (from the first words, counting, and colors video)?
items.explanation: Sumayaw means to dance! "Say yao" in the video is the word sumayaw.

items.prompt: How do you say "good day" in Tagalog? (Hint: maganda means beautiful, araw means day.)
items.explanation: Magandang araw means good day! Maganda means beautiful and araw means day.

items.prompt: Ate Pat said "maganda" means beautiful and "araw" means day. What does "maganda" mean?
items.explanation: Maganda means beautiful. It's the first part of the greeting "Magandang araw"!

items.prompt: What does "araw" mean?
items.explanation: Araw means day. "Arau" in the captions is the same word as araw — day!

items.prompt: How do you ask "what is your name?" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Ano ang pangalan mo means what is your name? Ano means what, pangalan means name, and mo means you.

items.prompt: What does "pangalan" mean?
items.explanation: Pangalan means name. "Ano ang pangalan mo?" is asking for your pangalan!

items.prompt: Ate Pat said "Ako si Ate Pat" to tell us her name. What does "ako" mean?
items.explanation: Ako means I. "Ako si Ate Pat" means "I am Ate Pat"!

items.prompt: Ate Pat said that when you talk to an adult, you should add a special word to your sentence. What is it?
items.explanation: You add "po" when you talk to an adult to be respectful, like "Magandang araw po"!

items.prompt: Ate Pat said you can answer "how old are you?" using your numbers. What does "sampu" mean?
items.explanation: Sampu means ten! You can say "sampu" when you are ten years old.

items.prompt: How do you say "I love you too" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Mahal din kita means I love you too. "Dinkita" in the captions is the word "din kita"!

items.prompt: It's time for you to go. How do you say "I'm leaving" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Aalis na ako means I'm leaving! "Alisnako" in the captions is the phrase aalis na ako.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog color word means red?
items.explanation: Pula means red. In the video, Ate Pat opens the red bag and says 'this bag is pula.'

items.prompt: What color is 'kahel' in English?
items.explanation: Kahel means orange. Ate Pat says 'this next bag is kahel' when she shows the orange things.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means yellow?

items.prompt: What does 'lila' mean?

items.prompt: What does 'berde' mean?
items.explanation: Berde means green. The coconut tree leaves and the calamansi are berde.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog color word means black?
items.explanation: Itim means black. The kalabaw (water buffalo) in the last bag is itim.

items.prompt: The bottom stripe of the Philippine flag is which color?
items.explanation: The bottom stripe of the Philippine flag is pula (red). It represents patriotism.

items.prompt: Ube is a purple yam. Which color word did Ate Pat use for ube?
items.explanation: Ate Pat says 'ube is lila.' Ube gives food a deep purple color.

items.prompt: The kalabaw is the national animal of the Philippines. What is a kalabaw in English?
items.explanation: The kalabaw is also known as a water buffalo. It is a hard-working animal found on farms.

items.prompt: The three stars on the Philippine flag are which color?
items.explanation: The three stars in the sun on the flag are dilaw (yellow). They stand for Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means red?

items.prompt: What does 'kahel' mean?

items.prompt: Which color is 'dilaw' in Tagalog?

items.prompt: Ate Pat says 'the small frog is green.' Which Tagalog word means green?
items.explanation: Berde means green. The small frog (palaka) is berde.

items.explanation: Asul means blue. Water (tubig) and the sky (langit) are asul.

items.explanation: Lila means purple. The woman's hat (sumbrero) is lila.

items.prompt: To say something has two colors, you use a Tagalog word that means 'and.' What is it?

items.prompt: What is turon?
items.explanation: Turon is a popular Filipino snack. It is a spring roll wrapper filled with banana.

items.prompt: What is inside turon?
items.explanation: Turon is filled with banana or plantains, and sometimes jackfruit and sugar.

items.prompt: How is turon cooked?
items.explanation: Turon is fried until it is golden brown and crispy.

items.prompt: What happens to the fruit inside turon?
items.explanation: The fruit inside turon gets caramelized from the sugar when it is fried.

items.prompt: Ate Pat counts to 10 in Tagalog. What is the Tagalog word for one?
items.explanation: Isa means one. It is the first number in the Tagalog count: isa, dalawa, tatlo...

items.prompt: What number is 'anim' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Anim means six. It is in the middle of the count to 10.

items.prompt: Ate Pat says 'we counted a 10 in Tagalog.' What is the Tagalog word for ten?
items.explanation: Sampu means ten. It is the last number in the count: ...walo, siyam, sampu.

items.prompt: Count with Ate Pat: isa, dalawa, ____, apat. Which word is missing?
items.explanation: After isa (1) and dalawa (2) comes tatlo (3), then apat (4).

items.prompt: Which word comes right after 'isa' when counting in Tagalog?
items.explanation: The count goes isa, dalawa, tatlo... so dalawa (two) comes right after isa (one).

items.prompt: Ate Pat says it is now her favorite time of the day. What does she call that time?
items.explanation: Ate Pat says 'now it's my favorite time of the day, merienda time.' Merienda is the Filipino snack time.

items.prompt: What is the name of the national anthem of the Philippines?
items.explanation: The national anthem of the Philippines is called Lupang Hinirang.

items.prompt: What reminds Ate Pat of the national anthem?
items.explanation: Ate Pat says that anytime she sees the flag of the Philippines, it reminds her of the national anthem.

items.prompt: What does 'bahay' mean?
items.explanation: Bahay means house. Ate Pat says 'in Tagalog, bahay means house' before singing the song.

items.prompt: The song about 'bahay' talks about different types of what?
items.explanation: The song is a Tagalog song about different types of vegetables.

items.prompt: In the body parts song, what does 'paa' mean?
items.explanation: Paa means feet. Ate Pat says 'paa is feet' before singing the body song.

items.prompt: In the body parts song, 'ulo' is your ___.
items.explanation: Ulo means head. Ate Pat says 'ulo is your head.'

items.prompt: What does 'tatlo' mean?
items.explanation: Tatlo means three. The song is about three little ducklings: tatlong bibe.

items.prompt: What does 'lobo' mean (from the children's songs video)?
items.explanation: Lobo means balloon. The song is about a kid who buys a lobo.

items.prompt: In the balloon song, what happens to the balloon?
items.explanation: The kid loses the balloon as it flies away, and he wishes he had bought food instead.

items.prompt: What does 'gagamba' mean?
items.explanation: Gagamba means spider. The song is about spiders that climb up a tree while it is raining.

items.prompt: What does 'ulo' mean?
items.explanation: Ulo means head. The head is made up of the skull, which holds our brains.

items.prompt: What does 'puso' mean?
items.explanation: Puso means heart. The heart pumps blood to the rest of the body every day.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means hand?
items.explanation: Kamay means hand. There are about 27 bones in the hand.

items.prompt: What does 'daliri' mean?
items.explanation: Daliri means finger. Everyone's fingerprint is unique - no two are the same.

items.prompt: Which body part is 'paa'?
items.explanation: Paa means foot. The toes on your feet help keep you balanced.

items.prompt: What does 'ilong' mean?
items.explanation: Ilong means nose. The nose cleans and warms the air we breathe.

items.prompt: When you feel sick, your family may feel your ___ to check for a fever. What is that body part in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Noo means forehead. Your mom, dad, lolo, or lola might feel your noo to see if you have a fever.

items.prompt: Ate Pat says the human body is made up of over how many bones?
items.explanation: The human body is made up of over 200 bones. The smallest is in the ear.

items.prompt: What don't babies have when they are born?
items.explanation: Babies are not born with kneecaps. They have cartilage that turns into kneecaps by age two.

items.prompt: Ate Pat says 'Paalam' at the end of the video. What does 'Paalam' mean?
items.explanation: Paalam means goodbye. Ate Pat says it when she leaves for her doctor's appointment.

items.prompt: What does 'bahay' mean (from the house vocabulary video)?
items.explanation: Bahay means house. Ate Pat shows a dollhouse and says 'bahay.'

items.prompt: What does 'bintana' mean?
items.explanation: Bintana means window. People in the Philippines like to keep the bintana open for air and light.

items.prompt: Which room is the 'kusina'?
items.explanation: Kusina means kitchen. Ate Pat loves the kusina because she tries Filipino recipes there.

items.prompt: You are in the kusina and want to find food. Where does Ate Pat say to look?
items.explanation: When you want food in the kusina, you can look in the pridyider (refrigerator).

items.prompt: You want to cook your food. What do you use?
items.explanation: Kalan means stove. Once you find your food, you can cook it on the kalan.

items.prompt: In the 'cuarto,' you can lay down in the ___ to sleep.
items.explanation: Kama means bed. When it is time to sleep, you can lay down in the kama.

items.prompt: To get comfortable, you can rest your head on an ___.
items.explanation: Unan means pillow. You can rest your head on an unan in the kama.

items.prompt: Which room is the 'banyo'?
items.explanation: Banyo means bathroom. It is a nice place to freshen up when you wake up and before bed.

items.prompt: In the 'sala,' you can get comfortable on the ___ or couch.
items.explanation: Sofa means couch. In the sala, the family watches movies and plays with toys.

items.prompt: If it is dark, you can turn on the ___.
items.explanation: Ilaw means light. If it is dark in the sala, you can turn on the ilaw.

items.prompt: What does "bago" mean?
items.explanation: In the video, Ate Pat shows a new phone and says "bago" means new.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "old"?
items.explanation: The video says "luma old," so luma means old.

items.prompt: What does "malaki" mean?
items.explanation: A tape measure helps you see if something is big or little. "Malaki" means big.

items.prompt: On a cold day you drink hot chocolate. Which Tagalog word means "cold"?
items.explanation: Ate Pat drinks hot chocolate on a cold day and says "malamig" means cold.

items.prompt: You use a towel to dry things that are wet. What does "basa" mean?
items.explanation: The video says towels dry things that are wet, and "basa" means wet.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "fast"?
items.explanation: A stopwatch tells if something is fast or slow. "Mabilis" means fast.

items.prompt: What does "mababaw" mean?
items.explanation: Water can be deep or shallow. "Mababaw" means shallow.

items.prompt: Keys can keep a door closed. Which Tagalog word means "closed"?
items.explanation: Keys open or close things. "Sarado" means closed.

items.prompt: What does "kali" mean?

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "right"?
items.explanation: In the review, Ate Pat pairs "right" with the Tagalog word kanan.

items.explanation: The first color bag is red, and the video says "pula" means red.

items.prompt: What does "kahel" mean (from the counting, colors, and animals video)?
items.explanation: The orange bag is "kahel" in Tagalog. A jeepney can be orange, or kahel.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "yellow" (from the counting, colors, and animals video)?
items.explanation: The yellow bag is "dilaw" in Tagalog. Mangoes are yellow, or dilaw.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "green"?
items.explanation: The green bag is "berde" in Tagalog. Coconut tree leaves are green, or berde.

items.prompt: What does "asul" mean?
items.explanation: The blue bag is "asul" in Tagalog. The top stripe of the Philippine flag is blue, or asul.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "purple"?

items.prompt: What does "puti" mean?
items.explanation: The white bag is "puti" in Tagalog. The sampaguita flower is white, or puti.

items.prompt: The kalabaw is the national animal of the Philippines. What is a kalabaw?
items.explanation: The video says the kalabaw is also called a water buffalo and is a hardworking farm animal.

items.prompt: What does "elepante" mean?
items.explanation: The elepante is the largest land animal in the world. "Elepante" means elephant.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "lion"?
items.explanation: Lions live in a group, or pride, of up to 30. "Leon" means lion.

items.prompt: What does "ahas" mean?
items.explanation: There are almost 200 kinds of ahas in the Philippines. "Ahas" means snake.

items.prompt: The Philippine eagle is the national bird of the Philippines. Which Tagalog word means "eagle"?
items.explanation: The Philippine eagle has a large wingspan and blue eyes. "Agila" means eagle.

items.prompt: What does "buwaya" mean?
items.explanation: A buwaya can be golden brown and gets darker as it grows. "Buwaya" means crocodile.

items.prompt: The smallest monkey in the Philippines is only 3 to 6 inches big and fits in your hand. What is it called?
items.explanation: The tiny monkey found in the Philippines is called the tarsier. It can fit in the palm of your hand.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "ant"?
items.explanation: The langgam is small but can carry very heavy things. "Langgam" means ant.

items.prompt: What does "paruparo" mean?
items.explanation: One of the largest paruparo is the Magellan Birdwing. "Paruparo" means butterfly.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "spider"?
items.explanation: A gagamba is nearsighted and can only see things up close. "Gagamba" means spider.

items.prompt: Bees help pollinate flowers, which is very important for the environment. Which Tagalog word means "bee"?
items.explanation: The buyog helps flowers grow by pollinating them. "Bubuyog" means bee.

items.prompt: What does "aso" mean?
items.explanation: Many homes in the Philippines have a guard aso. "Aso" means dog.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "cat"?
items.explanation: A pusa can sleep 12 to 14 hours a day. "Pusa" means cat.

items.prompt: What does "kuneho" mean?
items.explanation: A kuneho's ears help keep its body at the right temperature. "Kuneho" means rabbit.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "bird"?
items.explanation: There are over 700 kinds of ibon in the Philippines. "Ibon" means bird.

items.prompt: What does "pagong" mean?
items.explanation: The Philippine forest turtle has a yellow stripe on its neck. "Pagong" means turtle.

items.prompt: On a farm, a baka can be gray or brown. What does "baka" mean?
items.explanation: The video says a baka can be gray or brown. "Baka" means cow.

items.prompt: What does "kambing" mean?
items.explanation: A kambing eats weeds and gives natural manure on the farm. "Kambing" means goat.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "sheep"?
items.explanation: The tupa came to the Philippines during the Spanish era. "Tupa" means sheep.

items.prompt: You can usually find a bibe in the countryside of the Philippines. What does "bibe" mean?
items.explanation: The video says you can find a bibe in the countryside. "Bibe" means duck.

items.prompt: What does "kabayo" mean?
items.explanation: A kabayo can carry people or goods around the Philippines. "Kabayo" means horse.

items.prompt: What does "panahon" mean?
items.explanation: The video begins the weather lesson with "panahon," which means weather.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "storm"?
items.explanation: Typhoons are strong storms. "Bagyo" means storm.

items.prompt: What does "maulap" mean?
items.explanation: When many clouds fill the sky, the weather is maulap, or cloudy.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "lightning"?
items.explanation: Lightning can even be seen during a volcanic eruption. "Kidlat" means lightning.

items.prompt: What does "temperatura" mean?
items.explanation: The video says temperatures in the Philippines change with storms and land elevation.

items.prompt: The coolest month in the Philippines is January. Which Tagalog word means "cold"?
items.explanation: January is the coolest month, with a mean temperature of 26 degrees Celsius. "Malamig" means cold.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "ice"?
items.explanation: Ice candy is a frozen snack made from fruit juice. "Yelo" means ice.

items.prompt: What does "bahaghari" mean?
items.explanation: A double rainbow happens when sunlight is reflected twice in water droplets.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "sunny"?
items.explanation: The Philippines gets about 13 hours of sunlight a day, so it is often maaraw, or sunny.

items.prompt: Baguio City is a mountain town and is called the summer capital of the Philippines. What is its average temperature?
items.explanation: Because it is cooler, Baguio is known as the summer capital. Its average temperature is 18 degrees Celsius.

items.prompt: What does "kalikasan" mean?
items.explanation: Ate Pat loves taking in nature. "Kalikasan" means nature.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "forest"?
items.explanation: On the hike, Ate Pat walks through the gubat, which means forest.

items.prompt: What does "bato" mean?
items.explanation: Ate Pat says the big bato is a great place to take a breather.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "ground"?
items.explanation: The video teaches that the ground is called lupa.

items.prompt: What does "halaman" mean?
items.explanation: The halaman are all dried up because it is winter time.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "mountain"?
items.explanation: Ate Pat hikes up a bundok, which means mountain.

items.prompt: What does "ulap" mean?
items.explanation: The ulap floats in the sky. "Ulap" means cloud.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "sky"?
items.explanation: The video teaches that the sky is called langit.

items.prompt: Why are the plants all dried up in the video?

options.text: because the sun is too far

items.explanation: Ate Pat says the plants are dried up because it is winter time.

items.prompt: Where did Ate Pat go in this video?

options.text: on a hike up a mountain

items.explanation: Ate Pat says she is taking a hike up a mountain because she loves being outside.

items.prompt: Ate Pat says the name 'Tagalog' comes from a very old phrase. Which two words make up that phrase?
items.explanation: Taga means 'from' and ilog means 'river'. 'Taga-ilog' means 'people from the river', and that is where the name Tagalog comes from!

items.prompt: In the video, Ate Pat showed the Marikina River and taught that 'ilog' means...
items.explanation: Ilog means river! The people who lived near the river were called 'taga-ilog', or river dwellers.

items.prompt: What happened in 1937?

options.text: Filipino was declared the national language
Tagalog was declared the national language

items.explanation: In 1937, the government declared Tagalog the national language of the Philippines. Later, in 1987, Filipino became the national language instead.

items.prompt: What is the main difference between Tagalog and Filipino?

options.text: Filipino includes loan words from Spanish, English, and other languages
Filipino is much older than Tagalog
Filipino is only spoken in one city
Filipino and Tagalog are completely different languages

items.explanation: Filipino comes from Tagalog but adds loan words from Spanish, English, and other languages. Tagalog is the uninfluenced language.

items.prompt: Ate Pat said Spain influenced Tagalog for over 300 years. Which Spanish-influenced word means 'horse'?
items.explanation: Caballo means horse! Other Spanish loan words Ate Pat shared were radyo (radio), cuchara (spoon), and tinidor (fork).

items.prompt: Which foods came to the Philippines from Chinese culture?
items.explanation: Pancit and lumpia came from Chinese culture. Ate Pat also said beliefs like feng shui came from Chinese culture too.

items.prompt: The Philippines has three main island groups. Which one is up in the north?
items.explanation: Luzon is up in the north, Visayas is in the central area, and Mindanao is way down in the south. Tagalog is spoken in the Central Luzon area.

items.prompt: A friend asks you 'Kamusta?' How do you say 'I'm doing well' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Mabuti naman means 'I'm doing well'. Mabuti means 'good' and naman is an emphasis word.

items.prompt: You want to tell someone your name. How do you say 'I am Pat' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Ako si [name] means 'I am [name]'. Ate Pat says this is the common, conversational way to introduce yourself.

items.prompt: In Tagalog, when a number that ends with a vowel (like dalawa) comes before the word 'anak', you add...

options.text: 'ng' to the end of the number

items.explanation: Numbers ending in a vowel add -ng, so dalawa becomes dalawang anak (two children). Numbers ending in a consonant, like apat, use na: apat na anak.

items.prompt: What does the word 'po' do in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Po is a part of speech used to show respect. The closest English words to po are 'ma'am' and 'sir'.

items.prompt: Where do people think the word 'po' came from?

options.text: from the old word 'apo', which meant 'Lord'

items.explanation: Long ago, respected people in the community were called 'apo', meaning Lord. Over time it was shortened to po.

items.prompt: What is the 'mano po' blessing that children do for older people?

options.text: pressing the back of an older person's hand to their forehead

items.explanation: In the 'mano po' blessing, a young person touches the back of an older person's hand to their forehead to ask for a blessing.

items.prompt: Who do children learn to say 'po' to?

options.text: their parents, grandparents, aunts, and uncles

items.explanation: Kids are taught to say po to their parents, aunts, uncles, and grandparents. Adults also use po with elders and people in authority.

items.prompt: 'Nasaan po ang CR?' means 'Where is the bathroom?' In this question, what is 'po'?
items.explanation: Po is the second word in the question. The most common placement for po is as the second word of a sentence.

items.prompt: If you forget where 'po' goes in a sentence, what can you always do?

options.text: leave it out of the sentence
put it at the very start
add it at the end of the sentence

items.explanation: You can always add po at the end of anything you say, and it will still be respectful!

items.prompt: When you use 'po', the word 'ka' (you) must change to...
items.explanation: Ka (you) turns into kayo, the plural you pronoun. You would never hear 'po ka' together, because ka is singular.

items.prompt: How do you say 'thank you very much' with po?
items.explanation: Maraming salamat po means 'thank you very much'. Po goes after set phrases like this one.

items.prompt: What is the difference between 'po' and 'ho'?

options.text: 'ho' is less formal and 'po' is more formal

items.explanation: Both po and ho show respect, but ho is more informal and po is more formal. Ate Pat says she just uses po for everyone.

items.prompt: You want to say 'happy birthday' politely to your lola. Which one is the respectful way?
items.explanation: Maligayang bati is a set phrase, so po goes at the very end: Maligayang bati po!

items.prompt: What does it mean to 'conjugate' a verb?

options.text: to change a verb into a different form

items.explanation: To conjugate means to change a verb into a different form. We conjugate verbs for the past, present, and future tense.

items.prompt: For 'e' verbs like 'isara' (to close), where does the -in- go in the present tense?

options.text: at the very start of the word
between the first and second letters
between the second and third letters
at the very end of the word

items.explanation: For e verbs, the -in- goes between the second and third letters, so isara becomes isinasara (closing).

items.prompt: What does an actor-focused verb mean?

options.text: the action is done to the subject

items.explanation: In an actor-focused verb, the subject does the action, like 'the boy is playing' where the boy is doing the playing.

items.prompt: What does the pronoun 'siya' mean?
items.explanation: Siya means 'he or she'. It is gender-neutral, and even though it is spelled with a 'si', it is pronounced 'sha'.

items.prompt: Your whole family is eating together, and you are part of the group. Which word for 'we' should you use?
items.explanation: Tayo is the inclusive 'we' that includes everyone, like you and your whole family. Kami is the exclusive 'we' that does not include the person you are talking to.

items.prompt: What is the simplest Tagalog sentence structure?
items.explanation: In Tagalog the verb comes first and the pronoun goes after it, so 'I am cooking' is nagluluto ako.

items.prompt: How do you say 'I am eating' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Kain (to eat) is an um verb, so the -um- goes between the first and second letters: k-um-akain. Ako means I.

items.prompt: Which pattern makes a 'mag' verb present tense?

options.text: -um- between the first and second letters
-in- between the second and third letters

items.explanation: Mag verbs use nag plus a repeated first syllable plus the root, so maglakad (to walk) becomes naglalakad (walking).

items.prompt: How do you say 'they are sleeping' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Matulog (to sleep) is a ma verb, so it becomes natutulog in the present tense, and sila means they.

items.prompt: Ate Pat's Taglish tip: when you don't know a Tagalog verb, you can turn an English verb into a Tagalog verb by adding...
items.explanation: Just add mag to the English verb, like mag-drive! Then conjugate it, like nagda-drive ako (I am driving).

items.prompt: How many main verb types does Tagalog have?
items.explanation: Ate Pat says there are five main Tagalog verb types: mag, ma, um, in, and e verbs.

items.prompt: Which kind of verb is the most common in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Ate Pat says mag verbs are the most common type of verb in Tagalog.

items.prompt: What does the word "nagluto" mean?
items.explanation: Nagluto is the past tense of magluto, so it means cooked, like "nagluto ako ng kanin" (I cooked some rice).

items.prompt: To make a mag verb talk about the past, what do you add at the beginning?
items.explanation: For past tense, mag verbs use nag plus the root, like nagluto from magluto.

items.prompt: What does the word "tumakbo" mean?
items.explanation: Tumakbo is the past tense of takbo. In the video, "tumakbo siya" means he ran.

items.prompt: What does the word "sila" mean?
items.explanation: Sila means they. You use sila when you talk about more than one person.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "yesterday"?
items.explanation: Kahapon means yesterday. Ate Pat uses it to talk about things that already happened.

items.prompt: How do you say "will eat" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: For future tense, um verbs just repeat the first syllable, so kain becomes kakain.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "tomorrow"?
items.explanation: Bukas means tomorrow. Ate Pat uses it when she talks about the future.

items.prompt: In a simple Tagalog sentence like "nagluto ako", the verb comes...
items.explanation: Tagalog puts the verb first and the pronoun after it, the opposite of English.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "house"?
items.explanation: Bahay means house. Bahay ko means my house.

items.prompt: How do you say "my house" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: In Tagalog the object comes first, so "my house" is bahay ko.

items.prompt: Where do possessive pronouns like "ko" and "mo" go in a sentence?
items.explanation: Ate Pat says these pronouns never start the sentence; they always go after the object.

items.prompt: What does the word "aso" mean?
items.explanation: Aso means dog. Pusa means cat and kotse means car.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "delicious"?
items.explanation: Masarap means delicious. You can say "masarap ang pagkain ninyo" to say your food is delicious.

items.prompt: What does the word "masakit" mean?
items.explanation: Masakit means hurts. "Masakit ang ulo ko" means my head hurts.

items.prompt: Which word means "our" when everyone is included, like "bahay natin"?
items.explanation: Natin is the inclusive "our" — it includes everyone, like you, me, and the whole class together.

items.prompt: Which marker do you use when something belongs to ONE person, like "ni Maria"?
items.explanation: Use ni for one person, like "ang pusa ni Mario". Use nina for two or more people.

items.prompt: Which word means "this" or "these"?
items.explanation: Ito means this or these. Iyan means that or those.

items.prompt: Which word means "mine"?
items.explanation: Akin means mine. It is one of the pronouns that CAN go at the beginning, like "Akin ang kotse".

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "what"?
items.explanation: Ano means what, like in "Ano ang pangalan mo?" which asks what your name is.

items.prompt: How do you ask "what is your name?" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: Ano ang pangalan mo? asks someone their name. Pangalan means name.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "why"?
items.explanation: Bakit means why. You can use it like "Bakit ka umiiyak?" — why are you crying?

items.prompt: Which word for "because" is used the most in everyday talk?
items.explanation: Kasi is the most common and casual way to say because. Dahil is also used a lot, and sapagkat is very formal.

items.prompt: Which Tagalog word means "where"?
items.explanation: Saan means where, like "Saan ka pupunta?" — where are you going?

items.prompt: When a question uses "saan", the answer usually has the word...
items.explanation: When the question is saan, the response uses sa, like "Pupunta ako sa tindahan" (I am going to the store).

items.prompt: Which word do you use to ask where something is, like "___ ang susi?"
items.explanation: Use nasan (or nasaan) to ask where something is, and the answer uses nasa.

items.prompt: In the video, what do people in the Philippines call the bathroom?
items.explanation: CR means comfort room, and that is what many people in the Philippines call the bathroom.

items.prompt: What does "Bakit ka umiiyak?" mean?
items.explanation: Umiiyak means crying, so "Bakit ka umiiyak?" asks why you are crying.

items.prompt: What does the word "mamaya" mean?
items.explanation: Mamaya means later, like "Kakain tayo sa McDonald's mamaya" — we will eat at McDonald's later.

items.prompt: What does "kailan" mean?
items.explanation: The lesson teaches that "kailan" is the Tagalog word for "when."

items.prompt: How do you ask "When is your birthday?" in Tagalog?
items.explanation: "Kailan ang kaarawan mo?" means "When is your birthday?" In the video the answer is "Marso," which means March.

items.prompt: Someone asks "Kailan ang party?" and the answer is "Sabado." When is the party?
items.explanation: "Sabado" means Saturday, so the party is on Saturday.

items.prompt: In answers about the future, like "sa Sabado" or "sa Marso," what does the word "sa" show?

options.text: the time is in the past
the answer is about a person
the time is in the future

items.explanation: "Sa" is used before a time that will happen in the future, so "sa Sabado" means "on Saturday."

items.prompt: "Noong" in a response, like "noong nakaraang linggo," means something happened...
items.explanation: "Noong" talks about the past, so "noong nakaraang linggo" means "last week."

items.prompt: In Tagalog, when do you use "sina" instead of "si"?

options.text: when you talk about one person
when you ask about a place
when you talk about more than one person

items.explanation: "Si" is for one person, and "sina" is for more than one person, like "sina Nanay at Tatay."

items.prompt: "Kailan ka uuwi?" "Uuwi ako mamaya." What does "mamaya" mean?
items.explanation: "Mamaya" means "later," so "Uuwi ako mamaya" means "I am going home later."

items.prompt: What does "sino" mean?
items.explanation: "Sino" is the Tagalog word for "who," like in "Sino ang kumakanta?" which means "Who is singing?"

items.prompt: "Kanino ang itim na sumbrero?" "— Kay Jacob." Why do we say "kay" in the answer?

options.text: because the hat belongs to one person, Jacob
because the hat belongs to many people
because Jacob is not a person

items.explanation: We use "kay" because the black hat belongs to just one person, Jacob.

items.prompt: What does "kanino" mean?
items.explanation: "Kanino" is the Tagalog word for "whose," like "Kanino ang itim na sumbrero?" which means "Whose black hat is this?"

items.prompt: What does "paano" mean?
items.explanation: The lesson teaches that "paano" is the Tagalog word for "how."

items.prompt: The teacher asks "Paano magluto ng adobo?" What is she asking?

options.text: How much does the adobo cost?

items.explanation: "Paano magluto ng adobo?" asks how a person cooks adobo, because "paano" asks about an action.

items.prompt: To ask how tall or how big something is, you use "gaano" with a word like "katangkad" or "kalaki." What does "gaano" ask about?

options.text: the size of a quality, like how tall or how big

items.explanation: "Gaano" asks about the extent of a quality, so "gaano katangkad" asks how tall someone is.

items.prompt: "Magkano ang t-shirt?" means...

options.text: How many T-shirts do you have?
When did you buy the T-shirt?

items.explanation: "Magkano" asks about the cost of something, so "Magkano ang t-shirt?" means "How much is the T-shirt?"

items.prompt: What does "ilan" mean?
items.explanation: "Ilan" is the Tagalog word for "how many," like in "Ilan ang anak mo?" which means "How many kids do you have?"

items.prompt: "Ilan ang anak mo?" "— Tatlo." What does "tatlo" mean?
items.explanation: "Tatlo" is the Tagalog number three, so the answer means the person has three kids.

items.prompt: "Ilang taon ka na?" is asking...

options.text: How many kids do you have?

items.explanation: "Ilang taon ka na?" means "How old are you?" because "taon" means year.

items.prompt: What does "alin" mean?
items.explanation: "Alin" is the Tagalog word for "which," used when picking between choices like the red dress or the white dress.

items.prompt: In the question "Alin ang mas malaki?" what does "mas malaki" mean?
items.explanation: "Mas" makes an adjective a comparison, so "mas malaki" means "bigger."

items.prompt: The word "ba" turns a statement into...
items.explanation: "Ba" is a question word with no direct translation; adding it to a statement turns it into a yes or no question, like "Kumain ka ba?"

items.prompt: What is the general Tagalog word for sibling (brother or sister)?
items.explanation: Kapatid means sibling in Tagalog!

items.prompt: What do we call an older brother as a sign of respect?
items.explanation: Kuya is used to respectfully call an older brother.

items.prompt: What do we call an older sister in Filipino culture?
items.explanation: Ate is the respectful title for an older sister.

items.prompt: What is the word for the youngest child or baby sibling in the family?
items.explanation: Bunso refers to the youngest sibling in the family!

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for the oldest child among siblings?
items.explanation: Panganay means the firstborn or oldest sibling.

items.prompt: How do you say 'my brother/sister' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Kapatid ko' means 'my sibling'.

items.prompt: If Kuya is older brother and Ate is older sister, they are both your...
items.explanation: They are all your siblings (mga kapatid).

items.prompt: What value is shown when younger children call older siblings Kuya or Ate?
items.explanation: Calling older siblings Kuya and Ate shows paggalang (respect).

items.prompt: Which sentence means 'I have a sibling'?
items.explanation: 'May kapatid ako' means 'I have a sibling'.

items.prompt: When playing together happily, siblings show...
items.explanation: Siblings share love and care (pagmamahalan) with each other!

items.prompt: What does the phrase 'Mahal ko kayo' mean?
items.explanation: 'Mahal ko kayo' expresses love: 'I love you all!'

items.prompt: How do you say 'Thank you very much' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Maraming salamat' means 'Thank you very much'.

items.prompt: What is the common greeting for 'How are you?'
items.explanation: 'Kamusta ka?' asks 'How are you?'

items.prompt: How do you greet someone with 'Good morning' in Filipino?
items.explanation: 'Magandang umaga' means 'Good morning'.

items.prompt: What does 'Salamat' mean?
items.explanation: 'Salamat' is 'Thank you' in Tagalog.

items.prompt: When someone says 'Salamat', what is a polite reply meaning 'You're welcome'?
items.explanation: 'Walang anuman' means 'You're welcome'.

items.prompt: What does 'Mabuhay' express in Filipino?
items.explanation: 'Mabuhay' is a joyful greeting meaning 'Long live / Welcome!'

items.prompt: How do you say 'See you again' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Hanggang sa muli' means 'Until next time' or 'See you again'.

items.prompt: What word expresses pride and joy in Filipino?
items.explanation: 'Masaya' means happy and joyful!

items.prompt: When greeting someone respectfully, what word do we add?
items.explanation: Adding 'po' shows warmth and respect!

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'hot'?
items.explanation: 'Mainit' means hot (like the sun or soup).

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'cold'?
items.explanation: 'Malamig' means cold (like ice or winter breeze).

items.prompt: If soup is newly cooked and steaming, it is...
items.explanation: Fresh hot soup is mainit.

items.prompt: An ice cube or cold ice cream is described as...
items.explanation: Ice cream is refreshing and malamig.

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'warm / lukewarm'?
items.explanation: 'Maligamgam' means warm or lukewarm water.

items.prompt: How do you say 'The weather is hot today'?
items.explanation: 'Mainit ang panahon ngayon' refers to a hot sunny day.

items.prompt: What is the word for 'ice' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Yelo' is ice!

items.prompt: What is the word for 'fire'?
items.explanation: 'Apoy' is fire, which is mainit.

items.prompt: When drinking cold water on a sunny day, the water is...
items.explanation: Refreshing water is malamig.

items.prompt: Opposites in Tagalog are called 'kasalungat'. The opposite of mainit is...
items.explanation: Malamig is the opposite (kasalungat) of mainit.

items.prompt: What is the general Tagalog word for vehicle/car?
items.explanation: 'Sasakyan' or 'kotse' means vehicle or car.

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for a wheel/tire?
items.explanation: 'Gulong' means wheel or tire.

items.prompt: What do we call the steering wheel in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Manibela' is the steering wheel.

items.prompt: What is the word for the car door?
items.explanation: 'Pinto' is the door.

items.prompt: What is the word for the car window?
items.explanation: 'Bintana' means window.

items.prompt: What is the car seat called?
items.explanation: 'Upuan' is the seat.

items.prompt: What is the word for headlights or car lights?
items.explanation: 'Ilaw' means lights.

items.prompt: What is a bicycle called in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Bisikleta' means bicycle.

items.prompt: What do we call a driver who steers the car?
items.explanation: A 'drayber' drives the vehicle.

items.prompt: People riding in the car are called...
items.explanation: Riders are passengers (mga pasahero).

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for butterfly?
items.explanation: 'Paruparo' is a colorful butterfly!

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for ant?
items.explanation: 'Langgam' means ant.

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for honeybee?
items.explanation: 'Bubuyog' is a buzzing bee.

items.prompt: What is a dragonfly called in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Tutubi' is a dragonfly.

items.prompt: What is the word for spider (arachnid)?
items.explanation: 'Gagamba' is a spider.

items.prompt: What is a mosquito called in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Lamok' means mosquito.

items.prompt: What is the word for caterpillar or worm?
items.explanation: 'Uod' is a caterpillar or worm.

items.prompt: What is a housefly called in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Langaw' is a fly.

items.prompt: Which insect makes sweet honey?
items.explanation: A bubuyog (bee) makes sweet honey!

items.prompt: Which insect has colorful wings that flutter in the garden?
items.explanation: A paruparo has bright, colorful wings!

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'beautiful / pretty'?
items.explanation: 'Maganda' means beautiful or pretty.

items.prompt: What is the word for 'handsome'?
items.explanation: 'Gwapo' means handsome.

items.prompt: How do you say 'kind' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Mabait' means kind-hearted.

items.prompt: What does 'matalino' mean?
items.explanation: 'Matalino' means smart or clever.

items.prompt: What is the word for 'tall'?
items.explanation: 'Matangkad' means tall.

items.prompt: What is the word for 'strong' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Malakas' means strong.

items.prompt: How do you say 'You are beautiful' to Ate?
items.explanation: 'Maganda ka' means 'You are beautiful'.

items.prompt: What is the word for 'hardworking'?
items.explanation: 'Masipag' means hardworking.

items.prompt: What is the word for 'polite / respectful'?
items.explanation: 'Magalang' means polite and respectful.

items.prompt: When we describe someone with good traits, we use...
items.explanation: Words like maganda and mabait are descriptive adjectives (pang-uri)!

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'fragrant / smells good'?
items.explanation: 'Mabango' means fragrant or sweet-smelling.

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'smelly / stinky'?
items.explanation: 'Mabaho' means smelly or bad odor.

items.prompt: Flowers like sampaguita and roses are...
items.explanation: Fresh flowers are sweet-smelling and mabango.

items.prompt: What body part do we use to smell things?
items.explanation: We use our ilong (nose) to smell odors.

items.prompt: What is the verb for 'to smell / sniff'?
items.explanation: 'Amuyin' means to smell or sniff.

items.prompt: Clean laundry washed with soap smells...
items.explanation: Fresh laundry smells clean and mabango.

items.prompt: Trash or rotting food is described as...
items.explanation: Old garbage smells unpleasant (mabaho).

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'perfume'?
items.explanation: 'Pabango' is perfume or cologne.

items.prompt: How do you say 'It smells good!'?
items.explanation: 'Ang bango!' means 'It smells so good!'

items.prompt: Taking a bath and using soap makes us feel clean and...
items.explanation: A fresh bath makes us clean and mabango!

items.prompt: How do you say 'Happy New Year' in Tagalog?
items.explanation: 'Manigong Bagong Taon!' is the festive New Year greeting.

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'new'?
items.explanation: 'Bago' means new.

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'old' (objects)?
items.explanation: 'Luma' means old or used for objects.

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'year'?
items.explanation: 'Taon' means year.

items.prompt: What is the word for 'month'?
items.explanation: 'Buwan' means month (and also moon!).

items.prompt: What is the word for 'day'?
items.explanation: 'Araw' means day (and sun!).

items.prompt: What is the word for 'night'?
items.explanation: 'Gabi' means night.

items.prompt: What is the word for 'celebration / feast'?
items.explanation: A celebration is a pagdiriwang.

items.prompt: Round fruits on New Year are believed to bring...
items.explanation: Round fruits symbolize blessing and prosperity.

items.prompt: What do children do to make noise on New Year's Eve?
items.explanation: Children blow toy horns (torotot) happily!

items.prompt: What is the Tagalog word for 'happy'?
items.explanation: 'Masaya' means happy and cheerful.
